title: Right Rule, Wrong Layer
signal: The answer states real criminal doctrine but answers the wrong layer: violation instead of remedy, Miranda instead of voluntariness, attempt instead of completed offense, or larceny label instead of property-status variable.
student_move: Name the layer the answer occupies before judging its doctrine.
trap: Familiar law feels safe even when it does not answer the call.
confidence: HARD when call/layer mismatch is visible; ANCHOR-ASSISTED when trigger doctrine is needed.

title: Criminal Variable Matrix
signal: Choices split by actor, scope, remedy, timing, completion, mental state, causation, force, possession/title, or offense label.
student_move: Convert the answer set into the variable fight before using law.
trap: Student compares crime names or constitutional doctrines instead of identifying the tested variable.

title: First Live Gate
signal: One answer reaches a downstream result while another resolves a prerequisite gate.
student_move: Apply output → gate → actor → scope/timing → mental state/completion → remedy/result → ranking.
trap: A downstream true answer sounds substantive but is structurally late.
confidence: HARD for threshold/remedy/actor ordering; HEURISTIC or ANCHOR-ASSISTED for doctrine-specific outcome.

title: Tiny Criminal Anchor Deck
signal: Two well-built survivors remain, or the array is bare crime/constitutional labels.
student_move: Use the smallest anchor that resolves the already-identified variable.
trap: Turning Criminal Law into a doctrine outline.

title: No Mini-Outline Guardrail
signal: The explanation starts defining crimes or constitutional doctrines before identifying the answer-array variable.
student_move: Stop and restate: 'The choices are fighting over ___; the fact that resolves it is ___.'
trap: Legal explanation replaces construction analysis.

title: Wrong Route / Wrong Remedy
signal: The answer proves a constitutional violation but asks for the wrong consequence.
student_move: Ask what consequence the call asks for: suppression, dismissal, admissibility, reversal, immunity, or conviction.
trap: Illegal arrest/search/ID becomes automatic dismissal or universal suppression.
confidence: HARD STRUCTURAL when remedy mismatch is visible; ANCHOR-ASSISTED for precise remedy rule.

title: Item / Ground Matrix
signal: Grant as to X / deny as to Y, valid stop / invalid search, first private search / second state action.
student_move: Build item × gate × scope × remedy grid.
trap: One violation contaminates every item without a remedy rule.

title: Gate → Actor → Scope → Remedy
signal: Two plausible answers cite real constitutional doctrines.
student_move: Apply gate, then actor, then scope, then remedy.
trap: Jumping to suppression or guilt before the constitutional gate is set.
confidence: Mostly ANCHOR-ASSISTED; several hard structural pieces.

title: Tiny Constitutional Protection Anchor Deck
signal: The array is structurally clean but two answers remain well-built.
student_move: Use 4A search/scope/remedy, Miranda, voluntariness, 6A, confrontation, grand jury, double jeopardy, burden, immunity, and privilege anchors.
trap: Teaching a full Fourth Amendment or Miranda outline instead of resolving the identified gate.

title: Wrong Mens Rea / Wrong Defense Route
signal: The answer routes through completed offense instead of attempt, mistake of law instead of fact, intoxication instead of mistake, or strict liability instead of mental state.
student_move: Ask what gate controls the charge: act, actor, mental state, or defense.
trap: A nearby legal route is true but not operative.
confidence: ANCHOR-ASSISTED; hard only when answer visibly addresses a different actor, charge, or posture.

title: Actor / Defense Matrix
signal: Both/neither/A-only/B-only, guilty/not guilty crossed with reasons, or scenario quartets.
student_move: Convert choices into actor/charge/scenario × guilt/defense grid.
trap: Shared outcome answers hide actor-specific intent/control facts.

title: Route Before Guilt
signal: One answer jumps to guilt/acquittal while another identifies the controlling gate.
student_move: Apply voluntary act → actor/control → mental state → offense route → defense route → final guilt.
trap: Guilt label outruns actus reus or mental-state gate.
confidence: Mixed; hard for route order, anchor-assisted for effect.

title: Minimal General Principles Anchor Deck
signal: Two answers remain structurally clean or answer set is bare doctrine labels.
student_move: Use mens rea, attempt intent, mistake, intoxication, voluntary act, self-defense, regulatory liability, impossibility, insanity, and offense-label anchors.
trap: Treating insanity tests or impossibility as pure structure.

title: Wrong Degree Route
signal: Answer jumps to first-degree, second-degree, manslaughter, or no crime without routing causation, actor, mental state, or mitigation.
student_move: Ask which homicide gate the answer is using and whether that gate is live.
trap: Label-first homicide answering.

title: Degree Ladder / Causation Matrix
signal: First-degree/second-degree/manslaughter/no crime, murder/manslaughter/acquittal, causation yes/no, both actors/one/neither.
student_move: Convert the array into a ladder or matrix before using homicide law.
trap: Comparing labels instead of finding the splitting fact: death, cause, actor, intent, provocation, or intervention.

title: Baseline Before Degree; Highest Valid Offense Last
signal: One answer picks a homicide label while another identifies a prior gate.
student_move: Death → attribution → actor → mental-state route → mitigation/defense → highest valid offense.
trap: Lesser true label chosen in a most-serious call.
confidence: Mixed; route order structural, legal effect anchor-assisted.

title: Minimal Homicide Anchor Deck
signal: Bare homicide-label ladder or two well-built degree answers remain.
student_move: Use causation, malice, degree, felony murder, mitigation, self-defense, mistake/intoxication, transferred intent, accomplice, and no-duty anchors.
trap: Calling degree labels structurally decidable.

title: Wrong Inchoate Route
signal: Answer uses agreement for attempt, substantial step for conspiracy, payment/agreement for solicitation, or completed label where completion failed.
student_move: Ask which route is charged: attempt, conspiracy, solicitation, completed crime, or procedural sufficiency.
trap: True rule from neighboring inchoate crime.

title: Completion-Line Matrix
signal: Guilty/not guilty, completed crime/attempt, conspiracy/no conspiracy, solicitation complete/withdrawal effective.
student_move: Build route × completion point × stem fact grid.
trap: Offense label selected before identifying completion point.

title: Completion Point Before Label
signal: One answer picks a familiar label while another identifies why crime was incomplete or completed elsewhere.
student_move: Charged route → completion point → actor/party status → impossibility/approach → offense label → result.
trap: Most-serious ranking before threshold labels are excluded.
confidence: Mixed; completion order structural, rule anchor-assisted.

title: Minimal Inchoate Anchor Deck
signal: Short label quartet, impossibility item, or conspiracy-approach item.
student_move: Use attempt, impossibility, conspiracy approach, overt act, personal defense, protected victim, continuation, solicitation, and ranking anchors.
trap: Flattening common-law/MPC or legal/factual impossibility splits.

title: Wrong Crime Label Before Route
signal: Answer jumps to crime label before routing possession/title, force, entry timing, asportation, legal efficacy, or actor purpose.
student_move: Ask what variable separates these labels.
trap: Nearby crime label sounds right but lacks the route fact.

title: Label Quartet / Actor Matrix
signal: Larceny/embezzlement/false pretenses/no crime; robbery/larceny/attempt; burglary/attempt/larceny; both/neither/A-only/B-only.
student_move: Convert the array into property, timing, force, actor, and completion axes.
trap: Student chooses labels by recognition rather than variable routing.

title: Route Variable Before Offense Name
signal: Two answers remain because both name plausible crimes.
student_move: Property status → timing/concurrence → actor/purpose → force/asportation → completion → lesser-included/most-serious call.
trap: Familiar nearby crime beats the operative variable.
confidence: Mixed; route order structural, legal label anchor-assisted.

title: Minimal Other Crimes Anchor Deck
signal: Bare crime-label quartet or possession/title/force/timing split remains.
student_move: Use larceny, property/title, robbery, burglary, claim of right, forgery, receiving stolen property, kidnapping, accomplice, innocent agent, accessory, lesser-included, and impossibility anchors.
trap: Long theft-crimes outline replaces variable decoder.
